description: PostgreSQL wire-protocol proxy that shards by a key you name, keeps a directory of which region each key lives in, routes to that region, and relocates a key between regions while the application keeps reading and writing.
rules: Applications speak plain PostgreSQL to shahrah-proxy. There is no driver to install and no shahrah-specific code in the request path.
Every table must be declared in the topology file as either [policy.keys.<table>] (geo-partitioned by one key) or [policy.replicated.<table>] (same rows in every region); shahrah refuses to guess.
A statement against a geo-partitioned table that does not carry its key is refused. When the key exists but shahrah cannot see it (views, joins, ORMs), pass it in a comment: /* shahrah: key=7 */.
The console is a database named shahrah on the same port and answers only the simple query protocol. Reach it with psql, not with a driver that prepares every statement.
Console verbs like WHERE IS and RELOCATE are typed into psql, not executed as SQL from an application connection.
SHAHRAH_METRICS_LISTEN is unset by default, and without SHAHRAH_METRICS_PASSWORD shahrah refuses to bind anything but loopback.
Backend TLS is opt-in with SHAHRAH_BACKEND_TLS=require; any other value, including unset, means disable.
